name: Andorhal gate and yard people (gate clerk, guards, barley man, yard-reeves, magistrate, chalker, lamplighter)

physicalDetails.detail: Gate clerk (unnamed): young, already going bald on top, ink to the cuff of the right sleeve; pen hand shakes (nib chatters at the start of each line, steadies by the end); sits at a table just inside the arch with a board of wax seals with the yard's name inked under each. Wrote 'Proudmoore, Dalaran, Kirin Tor. Escort, Farstriders, three.' and Sylvanas's name copied off the foot of the pass into an open book anyone can turn back to. Reads 'Windrunner. Ranger-General. Which—' under his breath; Jaina cuts in 'My escort.'

Gate guards: two in the arch in militia leather with iron grain spikes arm-long and grooved down one side; a third on the wall walk with his back half turned; two more sitting by the trough inside. Cyndia counts five, four of them watching the wagons. The guard's line: 'Since the Exchange said.'

Barley man: Holt's carter ('Same as yesterday. You saw me yesterday.'). Chalker: a man in a brown coat and cap on an upturned barrel at the corner of the broad lane to the granaries, slate on his knee, a chalk mark for every wagon that turns down; looks up at the bows and chalks again (unclear whether for them). He packs up his slate when the lamplighter comes. Lamplighter: a boy with a pole, whistles the same few notes over and over.

voiceMarkers.detail: Clerk: curt, rote questions ('Whose yard?', 'Seal.', 'Business in the city?', 'Any business with the granaries? Buying or selling. A factor, the guild, a yard.', 'Carrying grain? Flour, meal, seed, malt?', 'For how long?').

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Admit the party on the pass. The clerk records them openly in the gate book.

howTheyAddressOthers.pattern: Clerk speaks to Jaina and reads Sylvanas's rank off the pass; no title for either.

knowledge.detail: Named offstage by Havel (all mentioned, none on page): Holt's (old Holt's boy now runs it; his men were with the father; 'you can leave Holt's out'), Fenner's (yard-reeve Coll Simmons, twenty years there, frightened of the loaders, will not say so), Garside's (yard-reeve Tarrant, drinks and owes at the Wheatsheaf, careless but simple; took a little of the new factor's grain at Lammas and stopped because the price was too good), Kett's on Tenter Row (small; shut his gate at noon, per Havel) and the old malt-house at the weir end that Garside leases (small). The Exchange granary is a fourth yard on Mill Lane. The magistrate freed Havel's two prisoners by dinner; the loaders' factor wrote to the town council about Havel's manners and the letter was read out in the hall. The factor's name is on the contracts and nobody at the Exchange has shaken his hand.

arc.currentPosition: Background figures. The gate clerk's book now carries Sylvanas's and Jaina's names; the barrel chalker's count sits on top of the gate's.
